exams.name: Written examination for adjuster license
exams.notes: Tests knowledge of duties and responsibilities of an adjuster and the insurance laws and rules of New Mexico. Developed and conducted under rules prescribed by the superintendent. No exam required for renewal or if applicant passed a similar exam in a state where already licensed.
exams.jurisdiction: state (superintendent may contract with outside testing service)
exams.quote: An individual applying for a license as an adjuster shall, prior to issuance of a license, personally take and pass a written examination.

required.quote: The superintendent shall require as a condition to continuation of an adjuster license that during the twenty-four months next preceding expiration of the current license period, the licensee has attended the minimum number of hours of formal class instruction, lectures or seminars required and approved by the superintendent.

period_years.quote: during the twenty-four months next preceding expiration of the current license period

available.quote: No examination shall be required: ... if the applicant took and passed a similar examination in a state in which the applicant is already licensed, subject to Section 59A-5-33 NMSA 1978.

requirements.value: Applicant must have taken and passed a similar examination in a state where already licensed. Residency requirement may be waived by superintendent under circumstances of necessity. Expedited licensure available under Uniform Licensing Act for out-of-state licensees in good standing.
requirements.quote: is a bona fide resident of this state, or of a state or country that permits residents of this state to act as adjusters therein, except that under circumstances of necessity the superintendent may waive the requirement of reciprocity

disciplinary_grounds.description: Permitting an unlicensed employee or representative to conduct business requiring a license
disciplinary_grounds.quote: an adjuster shall not permit an unlicensed employee or representative of the adjuster to conduct business for which a license is required pursuant to the Insurance Code

disciplinary_grounds.description: Paying commission or fee to an unlicensed person for investigating or settling claims in New Mexico
disciplinary_grounds.quote: an adjuster shall not pay a commission, service fee or other valuable consideration to a person for investigating or settling claims in New Mexico if that person is required to be licensed pursuant to the Insurance Code and is not so licensed

disciplinary_grounds.description: Undertaking adjustment of a claim when not competent or knowledgeable as to the terms and conditions of the insurance coverage
disciplinary_grounds.quote: an adjuster shall not undertake the adjustment of any claim if the adjuster is not competent and knowledgeable as to the terms and conditions of the insurance coverage, or which otherwise exceeds the adjuster's current experience

disciplinary_grounds.description: Having a direct or indirect financial interest in any aspect of the claim other than disclosed compensation
disciplinary_grounds.quote: an adjuster shall not have a direct or indirect financial interest in any aspect of the claim, other than the salary, fee, commission or other consideration established in a written contract

disciplinary_grounds.description: Acquiring any interest in salvage of property subject to adjustment without written permission from insured (for public adjusters)
disciplinary_grounds.quote: an adjuster shall not acquire any interest in salvage of property subject to adjustment; unless, in the case of a public adjuster, written permission is obtained from the insured

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to disclose to insured any interest in or compensation from construction, salvage, or repair firms involved in the loss
disciplinary_grounds.quote: an adjuster shall disclose to an insured if the adjuster has any interest or will be compensated by any construction firm, salvage firm, building appraisal firm, motor vehicle repair shop or any other business entity that performs any work in conjunction with damages caused by the insured loss

disciplinary_grounds.description: Soliciting or attempting to solicit an insured during the progress of a loss-producing occurrence
disciplinary_grounds.quote: a public adjuster shall not solicit, or attempt to solicit, an insured during the progress of a loss-producing occurrence, as defined in the insured's insurance contract

disciplinary_grounds.description: Referring insured to repair/service providers with whom the public adjuster has a financial interest or from whom compensation is expected, without disclosure
disciplinary_grounds.quote: the public adjuster shall abstain from referring or directing the insured to get needed repairs or services in connection with a loss from any person, unless disclosed to the insured: (a) with whom the public adjuster has a financial interest; or (b) from whom the public adjuster may receive direct or indirect compensation for the referral

disciplinary_grounds.description: Agreeing to any settlement without the insured's knowledge and consent
disciplinary_grounds.quote: a public adjuster shall not agree to any settlement without the insured's knowledge and consent

disciplinary_grounds.description: Representing or acting as a staff adjuster or independent adjuster while licensed as a public adjuster
disciplinary_grounds.quote: no public adjuster, while so licensed by the superintendent, shall represent or act as a staff adjuster or an independent adjuster

disciplinary_grounds.description: Adjusting a loss related to physical damage of a property on which the adjuster is also acting as a contractor
disciplinary_grounds.quote: An adjuster may not adjust a loss related to physical damage of a property on which the adjuster is also a contractor, acts as a contractor or is employed as a contractor

disciplinary_grounds.description: Accepting commission or fee for investigating or settling claims in New Mexico without being licensed
disciplinary_grounds.quote: A person shall not accept a commission, service fee or other valuable consideration for investigating or settling claims in New Mexico if that person is required to be licensed under the Insurance Code and is not so licensed.

bonding_required.quote: With application for license as a public adjuster, the applicant shall file with the superintendent a surety bond in favor of the superintendent in aggregate amount of not less than ten thousand dollars ($10,000)

definition_quote.value: "public adjuster" means an adjuster who acts or aids, solely in relation to first-party claims arising under insurance contracts that insure the real or personal property of the insured, on behalf of an insured in negotiating for, or effecting the settlement of, a claim for loss or damage covered by an insurance contract
